pdf_title: Integrated Oversampling for Imbalanced Time Series Classification
srcdet: All seven main datasets (split into 48 two-class 'apportions') come from the UCR time series repository [17]. Seven further UCR datasets (CBF, Synthetic Control, OSU Leaf, Fish, Gun-Point, Trace, ECG) were used in an additional comparison whose results are only given online, not in the paper.
crit: The datasets were chosen because they contain a large number of samples, to facilitate simulating scenarios of large class imbalance.
imbalance_creation: Started from seven 'balanced' UCR datasets. Multiclass sets (Adiac 37, FaceAll 14, 50words 50, SLeaf 15 classes) were made two-class by taking one class as positive and merging the rest as negative (one-vs-rest), giving several apportions per dataset (48 in total). The number of positive training samples was set to round numbers, no more than 50 percent of the available positives and no more than 50 per training set, to keep imbalance ratios high (7.6 to 60). Which classes were chosen as positive is not stated in the body text (Table 1 is an image).
normalisation: Each feature is min-max scaled to [-1, 1] using the training-data max and min, and the same values are applied to the test vectors.
split_protocol: Training and test data divided randomly, with all available samples in either the training or the test set (single random split; number of repetitions not stated). SVM (C, g) selected by log-scale grid search with five-fold cross-validation on G-Mean.
ir_definition: IM-ratio = number of negative samples divided by number of positive samples

evidence.quote: we constructed a total of 48 imbalanced two-class data apportions from seven balanced benchmark data sets in the UCR time series repository [17], as tabulated in Table 1.
seven balanced benchmark data sets in the UCR time series repository [17]
Out of the seven data sets, Adiac, FaceAll, 50words, and SLeaf originally contained 37, 14, 50, and 15 classes, respectively.
Note that SLeaf here refers to the “Swedish Leaf” data set.
with the highest being 60 for the Wafer data set and the lowest being 7.6 for the second apportion of the Wafer data set.
We examined our achieved results on the individual apportions for two particularly interesting data sets, Adiac and Yoga
Except for the FaceAll, TwoPats, and Yoga data sets which INOS was ranked as the second, fourth, and second places, respectively
We have also conducted comparison experiments on another seven UCR data sets including CBF, Synthetic Control, OSU Leaf, Fish, Gun-Point, Trace, and ECG
We have chosen these data sets since they contain large number of samples to facilitate the simulation of scenarios of large class imbalance.
we converted them into two-class data sets by selecting one class as the positive class and using the remaining classes to form the negative class.
we chose round numbers for the positive training samples and made sure that they do not exceed 50 percent of the total available positive samples.
For each training set, the number of positive samples is kept no more than 50 to simulate the scenario of rare positive instances.
We maintained high imbalance ratios (IM-ratios), i.e., the number of negative samples divided by the number of positive samples
For each set, the training and test data are divided randomly and all available samples are included either in the training or in the test set.
we perform logscale search for the best combination of (C, g), which gives the highest G-Mean in five-fold cross-validation.
we compared it with six oversampling methods (five different existing methods and our earlier SPO method) to balance the classes in the training data set separately
to linearly transform each feature hj to the range of [-1, 1], where h(Max)j and h(Min)j are the maximum and minimum of the j-th feature in the training data
The same scaling is also applied to all the test feature vectors in the testing scenario

notes: Tables 1-7 are images in the PDF; their contents were not readable in the extracted text. Dataset names were recovered from body text only; characteristics_columns left empty because Table 1 columns cannot be read, and ir_print_format set to 'not printed' only for the body text (Table 1 may print IR). Body text mentions some Table 1 values: Adiac apportions have 10 positives and length 176, Yoga length 426, Wafer length 152, TwoPats length 128. Name spelling varies: '50words' and '50Words'; 'TwoPats' and 'TwoPattern'. The paper calls all seven source sets 'balanced', even though four are multiclass and are binarised one-vs-rest. Page numbers are the printed journal page numbers (2809-2822; PDF page index = printed - 2808). Per-dataset results: Table 6 gives per-dataset results for INOS vs conventional methods; the oversampling comparison (Table 2) is averaged, and Tables 3-4 are per-apportion for Adiac and Yoga only. Results on the seven extra UCR datasets are only given online. The 'data cleaning' step (Sec. 3.4) removes synthetic samples as part of the method; it is not dataset filtering. How many random train/test splits were run is not stated.
